reader.requirement: At --std 85 every figurative constant other than ALL literal (ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES, SPACE/SPACES, HIGH-VALUE(S), LOW-VALUE(S), QUOTE(S), symbolic-character, each with or without the redundant ALL) that is not associated with another data item - a DISPLAY operand, a STOP literal-1, a STRING sending operand or delimiter, an UNSTRING delimiter - is a one-character string; the witnesses exercise only ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE in DISPLAY, STRING and UNSTRING.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(StopLiteralRemoved2002): the 1985 STOP literal SR1/SR3 screen runs only where STOP literal exists
Check(Constructs.StopLiteralRemoved2002): STOP literal passes at 85, is refused (removed) at 2002+

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition/ConstructRegistry/CobolVersion/IsAvailable over OperandText.cs, FigurativeConstants.cs, StringEmitter.cs, AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs, ConcatFolder.cs, StringUnstringBinder.cs: the DISPLAY/STRING/UNSTRING one-character arms consult no edition (StringUnstringBinder only passes ctx.Edition to diagnostic reporting); only the STOP literal path is edition-gated.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: STOP literal exists only at 85 (removed 2002), so the STOP arm of this rule has no latest-edition counterpart; DISPLAY/STRING/UNSTRING take the same code at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf02_01 exercises ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE in DISPLAY, STRING and UNSTRING only; not HIGH-/LOW-VALUE, symbolic-character, ALL-prefixed non-literal figuratives, STRING/UNSTRING delimiters other than SPACES, or STOP at all.

reader.notes: DISPLAY, STRING (sender and delimiter), UNSTRING delimiter and STOP keyword figuratives are each one character at 85 (OperandText.AsString's BoundFigurative arm, ConcatFolder.FigurativeChar for STOP). But STOP symbolic-character - a figurative constant (IV.4.2.2.2.3 item 7) usable wherever 'literal' appears, which STOP SR1 restricts only for ALL - is a parse error: stopStatement takes `literal`, whose nonNumericLiteral has no cobolWord arm (only concatOperand does, hence 'expected &'), so the one-character STOP arm is unreachable for that form.
reader.at-2023: same parse error COBOL5506 'expected &' (STOP literal is removed in 2002+, so a refusal is the right outcome there, though not the COBOL0902 removal diagnostic)
